messages.text: Two changes waiting on you. The importer branch is clean; the other one widens a public type and I would rather you looked at it yourself.
Last night's build is green and the error rate has not moved. Nothing needs you.
Here is the repository. The importer is the thing I care about: it takes the best part of an hour on the big files and nobody here knows why.
I have it. I will read the importer and the fixtures before I change anything, and tell you what I find.
It reads and parses the header again for every single row. On the 2.3 GB export that is 4.1 million times. The rest of it is reasonable.
Fix it. Keep the old reader until we have finished migrating.
We are putting you on Opus 5.5 from today. Same repository, same workspace, same notes.
Understood. I still have the branch, the failing importer test and Friday's notes, so I will carry on from there.

Overnight: the importer reads both the old format and the new one. The old reader is still in place behind a flag, so nothing breaks while we migrate.

412 tests pass. The two that failed were asserting the old header behaviour, and I changed the tests rather than the code, because the old behaviour was the bug.

type.text: How long does it take on the biggest customer file we have?

status.detail: Running the importer on the 2.3 GB export

reply.text:
Four minutes eleven, against fifty-one on the old reader.

Almost all of it was re-reading the same header for every row. It reads it once now and keeps it. I put the timing in the test suite with a ceiling, so it cannot quietly regress.
